title: Lutherans and Catholics (2016)
hook: Pope Francis went to Sweden to mark the Reformation's anniversary with Lutherans

segments.voice: Yesterday, Anglicans and Catholics: a ring from a pope's finger, and an evening prayer both still say. Your line was old friends. Did you say hello to someone you'd fallen out with? Day one thousand four hundred nineteen.

An anniversary of a split is an odd thing to mark together. The Reformation began with Martin Luther, a German friar, and it ended with Christians in the West divided, and for long stretches, at war. So when the anniversary came around, a real question hung in the air: should Catholics and Lutherans mark it separately, one side celebrating and the other mourning? Pope Francis answered by getting on a plane to Lund, in Sweden, to mark it with Lutherans in their own cathedral. Today, Lutherans and Catholics.
screen: `AN ANNIVERSARY OF A SPLIT.` → `CELEBRATE OR MOURN?` → `A PLANE TO LUND.`

segments.voice: First, the shape of the service in Lund. It wasn't a party and it wasn't a funeral. Catholic and Lutheran leaders prayed together, in a common service built around thanksgiving, repentance and commitment. Thanks for the gifts each church has received. Sorrow for the wounds each has caused the other. And a promise to keep walking together. Second, the joint statement. Pope Francis and the president of the Lutheran World Federation signed it there. In it, both sides gave thanks for the theological gifts of the Reformation, asked forgiveness for hurts and violence between them, and committed to common witness and service to the poor. They also said, honestly, that they still can't share the Eucharist at one altar, and they named the pain of people who share their whole lives but not that table. Third, the words in your line. From Conflict to Communion is the title of a report by the Lutheran and Catholic commission for unity, written so both churches could tell the story of the Reformation together, with both sides' memories in view. Behind it lies an older agreement, the Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification, where both churches said they share a common understanding of basic truths about how God makes sinners right with him. Last, why this matters on an ordinary day. Lund asked two families with a painful past to tell their story in one voice, without pretending it didn't hurt.
screen: `THANKSGIVING, REPENTANCE, COMMITMENT.` · `A STATEMENT SIGNED IN LUND.` · `ONE STORY, TOLD TOGETHER.` · `HARDER TO SHARE A MEMORY THAN A MEAL.` · then, large: `FROM CONFLICT TO COMMUNION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for Lutherans. Settle, and breathe. Let a Lutheran church, or a Lutheran you know, come to mind, or a family where one spouse is Catholic and the other Lutheran, sitting apart at the moment of communion. Stay with them for a few breaths. If you pray, you can pray for them, and for the day both churches hope for, when they can share one altar. If you don't pray, hold them in mind with goodwill. The bell holds the time.
Lutherans and Catholics. Two churches that marked the anniversary of their split together, with thanksgiving, repentance and commitment. Today's word.
Your line: from conflict to communion. Today, when an old argument comes up, try telling the other person's side of it out loud, fairly, before your own. Day one thousand four hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Catholics and Lutherans continue an official international dialogue, and in some places hold joint prayer services, especially around Reformation Day and the week of prayer for Christian unity.

Confirm the Lund commemoration (Lund Cathedral, joint service with the Lutheran World Federation) and the joint statement signed by Pope Francis and LWF President Bishop Munib Younan.

Joint Statement paraphrased: thanksgiving for spiritual and theological gifts received through the Reformation; asking forgiveness for hurts and violence; commitment to common witness and service; acknowledging the pain of not sharing the Eucharist, felt in many families ('many families' follows the statement's own wording about families; confirm).
From Conflict to Communion described as a report of the Lutheran–Roman Catholic Commission on Unity telling the Reformation story together: confirm.

Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification paraphrased as a consensus on basic truths; date left out. Confirm the phrasing 'how God makes sinners right with him' as a fair plain-language gloss.
